name: Emerson Levy
reasoning: Levy voted Aye on final House passage of HB 2002, 2023R1 (Chapter 228) on June 21, 2023 (House concurred in Senate amendments and repassed the bill) - the Reproductive Health and Access to Care Act, which expanded access to and legal protection for reproductive health care under a statute with no gestational limit - and voted Nay on all seven motions to refer or postpone that bill on May 1, 2023. In 2026R1 she voted Aye on HB 4127 (Chapter 63), directing the Oregon Health Authority to pay nonprofit reproductive health care providers with state-only dollars for Medicaid patients when federal funds are unavailable, i.e. public funding for abortion providers. Her campaign site commits her to protecting a woman's freedom to make her own health care decisions; she has never proposed a gestational cutoff, which is the line between chair 1 and chair 2.

name: Emerson Levy
reasoning: Levy was chief sponsor of HB 4113, 2024R1 (Chapter 35), requiring commercial insurers to count third-party copay assistance toward a patient's deductible, and she carried it on the House floor on Feb 20, 2024, voting Aye. She also voted Aye on HB 2010, 2025R1 (Chapter 4), which extends the health-plan premium, managed-care and hospital assessments plus the Oregon Reinsurance Program that together fund the Oregon Health Plan and subsidize the regulated private individual market. Her documented approach is making a mixed public / regulated-private system deliver affordable coverage, not replacing it with a public system (chair 1) and not narrowing help to only the poorest (chairs 3 and 4).

name: Emerson Levy
reasoning: Levy voted Aye on third reading of SB 611, 2023R1 (Chapter 226), which tightened Oregon's statutory cap on annual residential rent increases, and Aye on HB 2001, 2023R1 (Chapter 13), the roughly $200 million Affordable Housing and Emergency Homelessness Response Package that publicly funds housing production and imposes binding state housing-production requirements on cities; she was a listed member sponsor of HB 2001. In her own guest column in The Bulletin (March 10, 2023) she described the package as making affordable housing the top priority for local governments and state agencies. Statutory rent caps combined with large-scale public funding of new housing is chair 2 rather than chair 3's targeted-subsidy-only approach.

name: Emerson Levy
reasoning: Levy voted Aye on third reading of SB 611, 2023R1 (Chapter 226), which lowered the ceiling on annual rent increases under Oregon's existing statewide rent-stabilization law, and Aye on passage of HB 3054, 2025R1 (Chapter 387), which applied a tighter rent cap to tenancies for spaces in manufactured-home and floating-home facilities; she also voted Nay on the motion to refer HB 3054 to Rules, against derailing it. Tightening the cap and extending it to a previously separate class of tenancy is chair 2. She has not voted to remove the statutory exemptions, such as new construction, that chair 1 would require.

name: Emerson Levy

name: Emerson Levy

name: Emerson Levy

name: Emerson Levy

name: Emerson Levy
reasoning: Levy voted Aye on HB 4024, 2024R1 (Chapter 9), which established Oregon's first statutory campaign contribution limits and also requires reporting of the original sources of funds behind independent expenditures and disclosure on political advertising. In 2026R1 she voted Nay on final passage of HB 4018 (March 5, 2026), which modified those campaign finance timelines and permits corporations and labor unions to establish separate segregated funds operating like political committees. Voting for hard contribution limits and against loosening them places her at chair 2, past chair 3's disclosure-only position.

name: Emerson Levy
reasoning: Levy voted Aye on passage of HB 2107, 2023R1 (Chapter 492), which extends Oregon's automatic voter registration to Oregon Health Authority records and establishes a pilot issuing state ID and voter registration to adults released from Powder River Correctional Facility; she also voted Nay on the motion to re-refer that bill to Rules. Automatic registration of eligible citizens is the defining mechanism of chair 1. Chair 2's markers, no-excuse mail voting and expanded early voting, are already universal in Oregon and are not something she has acted to extend. Caveat: nothing in her record addresses online voting, the second clause of chair 1.

name: Emerson Levy
reasoning: In 2026R1 Levy voted Aye on HB 4114 (Chapter 58), creating a civil cause of action against persons who under color of law enter protected property without a warrant, and Aye on rejecting the minority report on it; Aye on HB 4111 (Chapter 57), which makes immigration status inadmissible in civil proceedings and adds immigration status to the statutory definition of law-enforcement profiling; and Aye on HB 4079 (Chapter 48), requiring school districts and colleges to adopt policies for when federal immigration authorities enter school property. name: Emerson Levy

name: Emerson Levy
